correctness.summary: Direct Bookstein-coordinate expansion identifies the normalized Neuberg–Pedoe pairing with the Poincaré half-plane formula for cosh distance; the Lorentz-form derivation via Heron's identity independently yields the same formula and supports all stated corollaries.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Classical Neuberg–Pedoe literature, Euclidean triangle hyperbolic shape-space literature, and the closest located Lorentzian-triangle Pedoe paper were compared. No located source states the exact Euclidean Bookstein-distance identity or its quotient and locus-distance corollaries; uninspected older review literature remains a residual risk.

value.summary: The result turns a classical two-triangle inequality into an exact intrinsic metric identity and provides closed formulas for unlabeled triangle-shape distance and for distances to equilateral, isosceles, and right-triangle loci.

limitations: The metric is the Poincaré/Bookstein hyperbolic metric, not Kendall's spherical/Procrustes shape metric.
Only nondegenerate Euclidean triangles are treated; degenerate shapes lie at the ideal boundary.
The labeled identity requires a chosen side correspondence; the quotient formula handles relabeling and reflection separately.
Originality is to the best of our knowledge; the full text of Mitrinović–Pečarić (1988) was not inspected and an equivalent older formulation may exist.
